one_liner: ARM NEON-tuned C++ image library (colour conversion, resize, warps) with an OpenCV-like API; first-party phone demos beat OpenCV 1.16-2.19x.
what_it_does: FlyCV (PaddlePaddle) is a lightweight image-processing library for on-device inference preprocessing: colour conversion (BGR/RGB/RGBA, gray, NV12/NV21/I420, BGR565), resize (linear, cubic, area), warp_affine/warp_perspective, remap, rotate, flip, crop, copy_make_border, some matrix math, drawing, and JPEG/PNG I/O via libjpeg-turbo/libpng, plus fused operators such as bgr_to_rgba_with_mask, y420sp_to_resize_to_bgr and normalize_to_submean_to_reorder. The API resembles OpenCV but is not a drop-in: it has its own fcv::Mat (constructed as width, height, FCVImageType, with colour order encoded in the type), enum codes such as ColorConvertType::CVT_NV122PA_BGR, and int return codes; optional C and JavaScript (Emscripten) interfaces exist.
how_it_is_fast: The hot kernels are hand-written NEON inline assembly for aarch64 and armv7: NV12 to BGR, for example, converts 16 pixels on two rows per loop iteration with ld2/st3 (de)interleaving and 6-bit fixed-point BT.601 coefficients (Y 74.5, V 102, 52, U 25, 129, truncating shift by 6), trading some precision for fewer instructions. Resize has dedicated exact 2x and 4x downscale kernels and separable fixed-point horizontal/vertical passes. Rows are split across a built-in spin-then-block thread pool (default 2 threads on multi-core CPUs, changeable with set_thread_num), and fused APIs remove intermediate buffers and passes; Android builds use -Ofast -ffast-math.
when_to_use: Android, iOS or ARM Linux camera pipelines that turn NV12/NV21 frames into BGR/RGB, resize and warp them before a neural-network runtime, especially on mid- and low-end SoCs where the first-party averages show the largest gains.

Apps where OpenCV's binary size is the problem: per-operator CMake switches (WITH_FCV_RESIZE, WITH_FCV_COLOR_CONVERT, ...) build only what you use, and Paddle's launch post claims 1.3 MB versus 15.9 MB for OpenCV for common operators (search snippet only).
Projects that already vendor another image library and need a custom namespace (-DFLYCV_NAMESPACE=...) to avoid symbol clashes.
Preprocessing chains that match one of the fusion_api functions (BGR plus mask to RGBA, NV12 resize to BGR, normalize plus mean-subtract plus HWC-to-CHW reorder).
when_not_to_use: x86 servers and desktops: the Linux x86 build is plain C unless you pass -DENABLE_AVX=ON (which then adds -march=native), SIMD selection is compile-time with no runtime CPU detection, and no x86 comparison with OpenCV is published.
When output must match OpenCV bit for bit: the README only promises essentially the same result, and kernels such as NV12 to BGR use 6-bit fixed-point coefficients with truncation.

Workloads needing operators FlyCV lacks: no smoothing filters (issue #208), no drawContour (#213), limited copy_make_border modes (#207), no video I/O (#177); resize rejects INTER_NEAREST although the enum defines it.

Several application threads calling FlyCV at once: issue #190 reports reproducible crashes inside the thread pool when multiple inference threads call it without a lock (closed without a visible fix).
Long-lived products needing support: last commit 2023-06-02, recent issues unanswered, and release download links reported broken (#214, #216).

integration.form: static lib or shared lib (CMake, BUILD_SHARED_LIBS); prebuilt release packages exist but their links are reported broken
integration.dependencies: none for core and img_transform; libjpeg-turbo, libpng and zlib for the media_io imgcodecs module (on by default, can be switched off); googletest, Google Benchmark and gflags are downloaded only for tests, benchmarks and samples
integration.min_toolchain: C++11; CMake 3.10 (3.12 with Xcode); Android NDK for Android builds
integration.platforms: Android armeabi-v7a/arm64-v8a and ARM Linux (NEON, optional SVE2 path), iOS, macOS (NEON on arm64, SSE/AVX on x86_64), Windows (SSE through AVX enabled by default), x86 Linux (scalar unless ENABLE_AVX), Emscripten/JS; Rockchip RV1109 code paths
integration.thread_safety: All calls share a process-wide singleton thread pool with one job slot (set_thread_num is global); a call made while another job runs falls back to serial execution in the caller, and issue #190 reports crashes under concurrent use from several threads.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — OpenCV-like function names (cvt_color, resize, warp_affine) but its own Mat type, image-type and enum codes, different argument conventions (issue #170 on warp_affine) and int return codes, so call sites must be ported

gotchas: Silent failures: cvt_color_neon logs and still returns 0 for unsupported conversion codes and for odd NV12 sizes (CHECK_CVT_SIZE returns from a void helper), and resize_cubic_neon leaves 4-channel RGBA/BGRA images untouched (the call is commented out) while returning 0, so INTER_CUBIC on RGBA on ARM yields an unwritten dst.

Code reading (not tested): the NEON YUV-to-RGB assembly loops (NV12/NV21/I420 to BGR/RGB/BGRA/RGBA) decrement the 16-pixel block count only after running the loop body and have no nn > 0 guard, unlike the BGR-to-YUV kernels; for widths under 16 the 32-bit count wraps and the loop runs far out of bounds.

Colour order lives in the Mat type, so in-place swaps such as cvt_color(src, src, CVT_PA_BGR2PA_RGB) fail the destination type check (issue #205 reported no effect); Mat is constructed as (width, height), the reverse of OpenCV's (rows, cols).
The Android toolchain file compiles the whole library with -Ofast -ffast-math, which can change float results (normalize, warp) and NaN handling.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick FlyCV over CompV or DeltaCV when the target is an ARM phone and you need a broad OpenCV-style preprocessing set (YUV conversion, resize, warps, normalize) in a small binary; for YUV conversion alone, sparkyuv or xxYUV have reproducible numbers against libyuv, and on x86 OpenCV itself or fast_image_resize are safer choices.
verified_claims_summary: The only readable comparisons are first-party screen recordings of an Android demo app at 1920x1080: NV12 to BGR 6.49 vs 7.55 ms (1.16x), BGR to RGBA with mask 9.69 vs 14.87 ms (1.53x) and a cvt_color + warp_affine + resize pipeline 29.6 vs 64.91 ms (2.19x), with OpenCV version, build, thread counts and compiler flags unstated; Paddle's launch post (search snippet only) puts the pipeline run on a Snapdragon 636 and quotes average speedups of 1.36x (Snapdragon 888), 1.77x (835) and 4.38x (625). The public Android sample links only flycv_static and the benchmark/ code times FlyCV alone, so the OpenCV side cannot be reproduced from the repo.
status_note: Abandoned since 2023-06-02 with unanswered issues, but Apache-2.0 and modular enough to vendor selected operators; audit the NEON kernels for small-width and unsupported-type paths before shipping.
